# Restore a stereo-preserving tautomer workflow

A cheminformatics workflow uses the supplied RDKit C++ source snapshot to
canonicalize tautomeric forms on a molecule that already carries stereochemical
annotations. One compact V3000 input loads successfully, but the
canonicalization step does not complete.

Run the public reproduction, inspect the source snapshot and the bundled
references, and repair the implementation so that this workflow completes on
the supplied input and remains coherent on other stereo-bearing molecules. Do
not hard-code the fixture, the generated probe, or the public report.

Work only under this task directory. The evaluation environment is Linux,
offline, and provides a C++ compiler, CMake, and Boost headers. You may modify
files under `source/`.

Run the public diagnostic with:

```bash
python reproduce.py
```
Repair the supplied RDKit source snapshot so a stereo-preserving tautomer
canonicalization workflow completes on the provided V3000 molecule and returns
a serializable molecule. The public reproduction is a diagnostic workbench for
the supplied input and source snapshot.
# Public Reproduction

Run from the task root:

```bash
python reproduce.py
```

The command builds a small C++ probe against the supplied RDKit source snapshot,
loads the supplied V3000 molecule, runs the stereo-preserving tautomer
canonicalization workflow, and writes:

```text
outputs/public_reproduction_report.json
```

The JSON report always contains a `status` field:

- `workflow_completed`: the workflow produced a finite, nonempty diagnostic
  observation.
- `pre_fix_expected_failure`: the workflow reached the molecule-processing step
  and exposed the public scientific symptom.
- `runner_failure`: setup, compilation, file access, timeout, or another
  infrastructure problem prevented the workflow from being evaluated.

Exit codes:

- `0`: `workflow_completed`
- `1`: `pre_fix_expected_failure`
- `2`: `runner_failure`
# Scientific and API Background

RDKit is a BSD-licensed cheminformatics toolkit used heavily in drug-discovery
workflows. For this task, the relevant public references are the project
documentation and the RDKit paper:

- H. Landrum, *RDKit: Open-Source Cheminformatics Software*,
  [Journal of Cheminformatics](https://jcheminf.biomedcentral.com/),
  2016. DOI: [10.1186/s13321-016-0168-3](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13321-016-0168-3)

Relevant public references:

- [RDKit project homepage](https://www.rdkit.org/)
- [RDKit documentation for `rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize`](https://www.rdkit.org/docs/source/rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.html), including `CleanupParameters` and `TautomerEnumerator`
- [RDKit Book](https://www.rdkit.org/docs/RDKit_Book.html), especially the sections on molfile parsing, SMILES writing, and stereochemistry
- The bundled source snapshot's comments and tests for tautomer enumeration, bond stereochemistry, and molecule serialization

The intended scientific behavior is representation-level consistency: tautomer
canonicalization may change bond orders while preserving chemically meaningful
state, and the returned molecule must remain internally coherent enough for
standard downstream serialization and inspection.

# RDKit
[![Azure build Status](https://dev.azure.com/rdkit-builds/RDKit/_apis/build/status/rdkit.rdkit?branchName=master)](https://dev.azure.com/rdkit-builds/RDKit/_build/latest?definitionId=1&branchName=master)
[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/10009991.svg)](https://zenodo.org/badge/latestdoi/10009991)


## What is it?

The [RDKit](https://www.rdkit.org) is a collection of cheminformatics and machine-learning software written in C++ and Python.

  * [BSD license](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/blob/master/license.txt) - a business friendly license for open source
  * Core data structures and algorithms in C++
  * [Python 3.x wrapper](https://www.rdkit.org/docs/GettingStartedInPython.html) generated using Boost.Python
  * Java and C# wrappers generated with SWIG
  * JavaScript (generated with emscripten) and CFFI wrappers around important functionality
  * 2D and 3D molecular operations
  * [Descriptor](https://www.rdkit.org/docs/GettingStartedInPython.html#list-of-available-descriptors) and [Fingerprint](http://www.rdkit.org/docs/GettingStartedInPython.html#list-of-available-fingerprints) generation for machine learning
  * Molecular database [cartridge](https://www.rdkit.org/docs/Cartridge.html) for PostgreSQL supporting substructure and similarity searches as well as many descriptor calculators
  * Cheminformatics nodes for [KNIME](https://www.knime.com/rdkit)
  * [Contrib](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/tree/master/Contrib) folder with useful community-contributed software harnessing the power of the RDKit


## Installation and getting started
